summaries.text: Backend engineer with 5 years building Python services at scale, most recently owning a payments ledger handling 40M transactions a month.
ML engineer focused on getting models into production: feature pipelines, evaluation harnesses, and the boring reliability work that makes them useful.
Full-stack engineer who prefers backend, comfortable owning a feature from schema to deploy.

bullets.text: Owned the double-entry ledger service processing 40M transactions per month, cutting reconciliation breaks from 1.2% to 0.03% over two quarters.
Redesigned the settlement pipeline around idempotency keys and an outbox table, eliminating the duplicate-payout class of incidents entirely.
Cut p99 API latency from 890ms to 210ms by replacing a chatty ORM access pattern with a single materialised view refresh.
Introduced contract tests between the ledger and four consuming services, taking cross-team breakages from roughly weekly to two in a year.
Migrated the service from a hand-rolled deploy script to Terraform and ArgoCD, dropping deploy time from 25 minutes to under 4.
Mentored two junior engineers through their first on-call rotations and wrote the runbook the team still uses.
Built an internal FastAPI service exposing ledger snapshots to the finance team, replacing a weekly manual CSV export.
Built the ingestion pipeline for satellite imagery metadata, handling 8TB a week through Airflow and S3.
Shipped a crop-classification model into production behind a gRPC service, moving it from a notebook to a versioned, monitored endpoint.
Wrote the evaluation harness the ML team used for every model release, including per-region slices that caught a 14-point accuracy drop before launch.
Reduced AWS spend 38% by moving cold imagery to Glacier and right-sizing the Airflow workers.
Added structured logging and tracing across six services with OpenTelemetry, cutting mean time to diagnose from hours to minutes.
Worked directly with two agronomist customers to turn vague accuracy complaints into a concrete labelling-error hypothesis, which held.
Built REST APIs in Django for a logistics dashboard used by 300 warehouse staff daily.
Replaced nightly batch stock reconciliation with an event-driven Celery workflow, taking stock accuracy from 92% to 99.4%.
Wrote the team's first integration test suite, going from zero automated coverage to 71% on the critical path.
Built an internal React dashboard for warehouse throughput, still in use three years later.

projects.name: ledgerfuzz
projects.description: Property-based fuzzer for double-entry accounting invariants.

bullets.text: Property-based fuzzer that generates transaction sequences and asserts double-entry invariants hold; found three bugs in two open-source ledger libraries.
340 stars, used in CI by two payments startups.
A deliberately minimal 400-line retrieval-augmented generation implementation written to teach the moving parts without a framework.
Wrote an accompanying post on chunking trade-offs that reached the front page of Hacker News.

projects.name: shiftplan
projects.description: Constraint-solver shift scheduler for a local clinic.

bullets.text: Built a constraint-solver shift scheduler for a 40-person clinic, replacing a spreadsheet that took the manager a day a week.

education.detail: Thesis on approximate nearest-neighbour search. GPA 8.7/10.

answer_bank.question: Do you require visa sponsorship?
answer_bank.answer: I am an Indian citizen and would require sponsorship for roles based outside India.

answer_bank.question: What are your salary expectations?
answer_bank.answer: Open to discussing based on the full package and level; happy to align with your band for the role.

answer_bank.question: Why do you want to work here?
answer_bank.answer: I want to work on systems where correctness is load-bearing rather than aspirational — payments, infrastructure, or ML that people actually depend on.

answer_bank.question: Describe a difficult technical problem you solved.
answer_bank.answer: The duplicate-payout incidents at Fintrail: the fix was not a patch but a redesign around idempotency keys and an outbox table, which required convincing three teams to change their integration.
